query: Consider the following context: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications. In that context, which method can be used for tuning the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Controlling the alloy’s specific elemental composition (i.e., compositional tuning) will modify the local magnetic exchange interactions and structural disorder, thereby shifting the magnetic transition temperature and modulating the magnitude of the magnetocaloric effect in non‐equiatomic HEAs.
generation.material_initial_state: A non‐equiatomic high-entropy alloy with a disordered solid-solution structure.
generation.intervention: Systematically vary the relative concentrations of the constituent elements (atomic substitution) during synthesis.
generation.conditions: Experiments conducted under controlled synthesis and measurement conditions at ambient pressure and on low-dimensional (e.g., thin film or nanostructured) HEA samples.
generation.structural_mediator: Local atomic arrangement and chemical short-range order, which alter the magnetic exchange pathways and interatomic distances.
generation.mechanism: Changes in composition adjust the valence electron concentration and modify magnetic interactions, which affect the magnetic ordering temperature; these shifts in ordering also influence the entropy change under applied magnetic fields, thus modifying the magnetocaloric response.
generation.predicted_outcome: A systematic variation in composition will lead to a predictable shift in the magnetic transition temperature and corresponding changes in the magnitude of the magnetocaloric effect, although the precise quantitative changes are uncertain.
generation.baseline: The initial non-equiatomic HEA with its baseline magnetic and magnetocaloric properties measured prior to compositional changes.
generation.boundary: Results are expected to be observable in low-dimensional samples and may not directly extend to bulk materials or to alloys with nearly equiatomic compositions.
generation.uncertainty: While the direction of the effect (i.e., shift in transition temperature and magnetocaloric effect modulation) is supported by general principles of magnetic exchange in disordered alloys, the exact magnitude of these changes remains uncertain without further experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of non-equiatomic HEA samples with systematically varied elemental ratios. Measure their magnetic transition temperatures using techniques such as AC/DC magnetometry, and evaluate the magnetocaloric response via direct calorimetric measurements under applied magnetic fields.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the compositional variations do not result in statistically significant shifts in the magnetic transition temperature or consistent modulation of the magnetocaloric effect beyond experimental error, then the hypothesis that compositional tuning can effectively control these properties in non-equiatomic HEAs would be falsified.
